title: Slovakia's Budget Gamble: High Deficits, Rising Debt · 16 Oct
keywords: Slovakia, budget deficit, fiscal policy, public debt, railway strike, wage dispute, inflation, ŽSR, EU fiscal rules, public sector wages, cost of living, Central Europe
notes: Slovakia's parliament has approved a 2027 budget projecting a general-government deficit of 4.94 percent of GDP, higher than the previous year's already elevated shortfall and part of a fiscal path that would push public debt toward 71.8 percent of GDP by 2029. At the same time, railway unions have declared a strike alert after wage negotiations collapsed, exposing a sharp contradiction at the heart of government policy. Together, the two developments raise a question that extends well beyond Bratislava: who bears the cost of stability when inflation has slowed but debt and living costs remain high?
